did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah was shown the vision of two baskets after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported Jeconiah king of Judah, the officials of Judah, and the craftsmen from Jerusalem to Babylon.
Did you know? One basket contained very good figs, like early-ripening figs, while the other contained very bad figs that could not be eaten.
Did you know? The LORD asked Jeremiah what he saw, and Jeremiah replied that he saw figs—very good ones on the one hand and very bad ones on the other.
Did you know? After the vision was described, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, beginning the prophetic interpretation of the vision of the figs.
Did you know? The LORD compared the exiles of Judah who had been sent to the land of the Chaldeans to the good figs, making clear that their exile would be for their good.
Did you know? The LORD promised to watch over the exiles for their good, bring them back to the land, and build them up and plant them there.
Did you know? According to the prophecy, the exiles would receive a heart that would know the LORD, they would be his people, and they would return to him with all their heart.
Did you know? The bad figs represented Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, the remnant of Jerusalem, and those living in the land of Egypt.
Did you know? Those represented by the bad figs would become a disgrace, a byword, an object of ridicule, and a curse in all the places where they were banished.
Did you know? The punishments mentioned at the end of the chapter are sword, famine, and plague, until they are destroyed from the land given to them and their ancestors.
